headline: Elon Musk replied to an AI-generated clip of Nvidia's Jensen Huang dancing by joking that this is why RAM is so expensive.
score_reason: Pool score 2 lowered by 1: Musk's reply was posted on Sunday 4 Oct 2026, before the window, and it is a joke with no news beyond it.
importance_line: Higher RAM prices reach anyone buying a computer, and Primetimer, citing NZXT, ties them to AI demand; Musk's post is a joke, and neither it nor the report shows how much of the rise AI explains.
summary: Primetimer reports that on Sunday 4 Oct 2026 Elon Musk replied to a post on X by the account @bqlsj, which showed an AI-generated video of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang dancing to an AI-written version of Michael Jackson's "Beat It" while AI-made tech leaders, Musk among them, cheer; Musk joked that this is why RAM (computer memory) is so expensive. Primetimer links the joke to a real trend, citing the PC maker NZXT: AI data centres are absorbing much of the world's memory output, and makers such as Samsung and Micron are favouring HBM, a fast memory for AI hardware, over standard RAM.
notes: Reply story (Musk answers @bqlsj); the original post's date is not given and it was not carried in our earlier editions. Musk's wording comes from Primetimer's headline because the embedded tweet is missing from the page text. Event dated Sunday 4 Oct 2026, a day before the window; score lowered by 1.
